proposals.before: After the Deposed Emperor took the throne, envoys came and went incessantly, too many to count, so those of low rank are generally omitted. Wang Ban is recorded because he was unable to proceed.
proposals.after: After the Fleeing Emperor took the throne, envoys came and went incessantly, too many to count, so those of low rank are generally omitted. Wang Ban is recorded because he was unable to proceed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 出帝 is the Fleeing Emperor (Emperor Chu), not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝); the idiomatic English misidentifies the ruler.

proposals.before: The Deposed Emperor had promised to spare him, but later ordered Li Shouzhen to have him killed; for that reason the text does not say he was executed.
proposals.after: The Fleeing Emperor had promised to spare him, but later ordered Li Shouzhen to have him killed; for that reason the text does not say he was executed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 出帝 should be Fleeing Emperor, not Deposed Emperor; 廢帝 is a different Later Tang ruler mentioned elsewhere.

proposals.before: On renwu Li Zhou, former commissioner of Jingnan, stayed to guard the Eastern Capital while Jing Yanguang took command of the imperial camp.
proposals.after: On renwu Li Zhou, former commissioner of the Jingnan (靜難) army, stayed to guard the Eastern Capital while Jing Yanguang took command of the imperial camp.
proposals.reason: 靜難軍 is the Jingnan/Jingnan command at Binzhou; rendering it as Jingnan without the Chinese risks confusion with 荊南, but more clearly the prior office is 靜難 not a place name Jingnan alone. Prefer marking the army name explicitly.

proposals.before: On jiayin the Goryeo envoy Taixiang arrived.
proposals.after: On jiayin a Goryeo grand minister (taesang) envoy arrived.
proposals.reason: 太相 is a Goryeo official title (taesang), not a personal name Taixiang.

proposals.before: On jichou Li Shouzhen was named overall commander of the field army, with Huang Fuyu of Yicheng as his deputy.
proposals.after: On jichou Li Shouzhen was named overall commander of the field army, with Huangfu Yu of Yicheng as his deputy.
proposals.reason: 皇甫 is the compound surname Huangfu; 皇甫遇 is Huangfu Yu, not “Huang Fuyu.”

proposals.before: On jichou Li Shouzhen was made overall commander of the campaign headquarters, and Yicheng army commissioner Huang Fuyu was made his deputy.
proposals.after: On jichou Li Shouzhen was made overall commander of the campaign headquarters, and Yicheng army commissioner Huangfu Yu was made his deputy.
proposals.reason: Same compound-surname error: 皇甫遇 should be rendered Huangfu Yu.

proposals.before: Although the Deposed Emperor was still alive, Jin had already fallen, so the text writes “destroyed.”
proposals.after: Although the Fleeing Emperor was still alive, Jin had already fallen, so the text writes “destroyed.”
proposals.reason: 出帝 is rendered “Fleeing Emperor” consistently elsewhere in this chapter; “Deposed Emperor” is an inconsistent alternate.

proposals.before: The Fleeing Emperor’s accession was not legitimate, and he severed ties with the man who bore him.
proposals.after: The Fleeing Emperor’s accession was not legitimate, and he severed ties with the one who begot him.
proposals.reason: 所生 refers to the birth parent (here the father); “bore him” is the wrong English verb for a father.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 至出帝立; 出帝 is the Fleeing Emperor, not 廢帝 (Deposed Emperor). The before text mislabels the ruler; the proposed Fleeing Emperor matches the Chinese and the chapter’s own title usage.
Focus unit subjects 出帝 as the one who promised Yang Guangyuan’s life then ordered him killed. Rendering him Deposed Emperor confuses 出帝 with 廢帝; Fleeing Emperor is the accurate English for 出帝.
前靜難軍節度使 is already fairly rendered as former commissioner of Jingnan; inserting Chinese 靜難 and “army” is stylistic disambiguation, not correction of a semantic error in the English.

Focus unit 高麗使太相來 names only the Goryeo office 太相, with no personal name; parallel s0074 names Jin Renfeng with a title. Treating 太相 as the personal name Taixiang invents an envoy; the proposed title reading (taesang/grand minister) matches the Chinese.
Focus unit has 皇甫遇; 皇甫 is the compound surname Huangfu and 遇 is Yu. Splitting as Huang Fuyu invents a wrong personal name; Huangfu Yu restores the correct reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 義成軍節度使皇甫遇為副

decisions.reason: The literal field of the same unit likewise mis-splits 皇甫遇 as Huang Fuyu; Huangfu Yu correctly reflects the compound surname and given name.
Focus unit 出帝雖存 again names 出帝. Deposed Emperor is the wrong English label; Fleeing Emperor matches 出帝 and the corrected rendering elsewhere in the chapter.

Focus unit 絕其所生, with s0184 identifying Jingru as 出帝父, refers to the birth father. English “bore him” is the wrong verb for a father; “begot him” correctly marks paternal parentage without changing the Chinese sense.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0007 shows the alternate English Deposed Emperor for 出帝 was invented by the bad idiomatic rendering; s0206 supports only 出帝, already claimed correctly as Fleeing Emperor in c0224.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001/r0002 restore 出帝 as Fleeing Emperor; the extracted alternate-name Deposed Emperor was a mistranslation of the same evidence units and must be corrected rather than left as a false alias.

Accepted r0005/r0006 show the English personal name Huang Fuyu was a bad split of compound surname 皇甫; the underlying person 皇甫遇 remains, so the English value is revised to Huangfu Yu (zh and pinyin already correct).
